&api-questions;
The nbfx Output API provides the pure-JavaFX output consoles: the OutputConsole service and the ConsolePanel handles, shown by the Output view.
Build, run and test activities write into named consoles obtained from the OutputConsole service. Each console accumulates text thread-safely and marshals it to the JavaFX Application Thread; the Output view shows the consoles as tabs, each a read-only rich text area over a model of the console lines, beside a tool bar acting on the selected console. An activity tells its console how to run it again and how to stop it; the tool bar and the context menu of the console offer both. The default implementation is registered with @ServiceProvider; the view with @ViewRegistration.
Build and Run commands stream the tool output into a console.
A user opens the Output view to read the streaming output.
A user runs a build again, or stops it, from its console.
A user copies or saves the output, wraps it or changes its font size.
The console registry, the line model and the view are unit-tested. The API is under development.
A JDK is required only to compile; JavaFX is provided by the runtime.
Only org.netbeans.modules.nbfx.platform.output is public.
OutputConsole is resolved from the global Lookup.
ConsoleOutput is registered as the OutputConsole service.
The Output view is registered under NbFx/Views.
None.
The module's preferences keep the font size and the line wrapping of the consoles.
Console appends are safe from any thread; they are marshalled to the JavaFX Application Thread. The Output view is built on the JavaFX Application Thread.
No console is created until something writes to it.
No code runs on exit.
No special requirements.
